channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Esforço concentrado no Senado dependerá de nova reunião entre Lula e Alcolumbre; governo vê dificuldade para aprovar pautas
item.description: The approval of the government's priority agendas in the Senate depends on a new meeting between Lula and Alcolumbre, as the first encounter was seen only as an initial step in their rapprochement. While relations with the Chamber are favorable, there is pessimism in the Senate about voting in August on key proposals such as the PEC to end the 6x1 work scale and the Public Security PEC. The government is also monitoring two Chamber initiatives: the MP that abolished the 'tax on small packages' and the project using extra oil revenue to curb fuel price increases, though business groups are mobilizing to invalidate the MP before its September deadline.

item.title: Polícia investiga grupo que planejava ataques em Brasília durante as eleições
item.description: The Federal District Civil Police is investigating a group that planned attacks in Brasília during the 2026 elections, including building invasions, target selection, tactical training, and recruitment across multiple states. Operation Rede Interrompida led to the arrest of eight individuals aged 19 to 31, located in Santa Catarina, Paraná, São Paulo, Pernambuco, and Rio Grande do Sul, with support from state civil police forces. The investigation, triggered by a Ciberlab report, includes seized electronic devices, maps, 3D building models, and manuals for manufacturing explosive devices.

item.title: Caiado propõe criação de lei de terrorismo doméstico e agência policial com países vizinhos
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado proposed the creation of a domestic terrorism law to classify militias and criminal organizations like the PCC, announced on Monday, October 8, 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen the fight against organized crime through specific legislation and police cooperation with neighboring countries. Caiado also suggested forming a multinational police agency to enhance effectiveness against armed groups operating across borders.

item.title: Programa de governo de Lula: balelas, lorotas e mentiras
item.description: The text criticizes Lula's government program, claiming it contains false promises ('balelas'), misleading statements ('lorotas'), and deliberate lies. It argues that despite Lula and the PT having governed for nearly two decades (except for 5 years and 7 months), Brazil faces fiscal deterioration, with gross debt reaching 82% of GDP and exceptional spending outside the fiscal ceiling, disguised as 'puxadinhos'. The new fiscal framework is portrayed as a fallacy that masks real spending increases and excessive indebtedness.

item.title: Lulistas criticam Moraes por barrar visita a Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Lula’s allies criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for blocking a visit by Jair Bolsonaro’s sons to him on Father’s Day, arguing the decision reinforces the Bolsonaro clan’s victimhood narrative. They believe the restriction could politically benefit Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign by providing fresh material for claims of persecution against the STF.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula volta a ampliar vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º e no 2º turno
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula slightly regaining his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round (40% to 35%) and second round (47% to 44%), though results remain within the margin of error, indicating a technical tie. Despite stable raw numbers, the shift was more pronounced among Flávio’s supporters, benefiting Lula. High rejection rates persist — 50% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 48% for Lula — underscoring the relevance of the 'lesser evil' vote in the election.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Apostas para equipe econômica em eventual Lula 4 apontam também para ‘pós-Lula’
item.description: The economic team for a potential fourth Lula term points to continuity of the current administration, with gradual fiscal adjustments and the political strengthening of Fernando Haddad as a potential Chief of Staff and Lula’s political heir. Dario Durigan is favored for Finance, while Bruno Moretti of Planning is seen as a 'superminister' in budget affairs, praised by Lula for balancing fiscal limits with funding for new public policies. The scenario reflects stability over the 2022 contest, focusing on consolidating results and preparing for the 'post-Lula' era.

item.title: Alcolumbre aproxima centrão de Lula e afasta apoio a Flávio
item.description: Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), Senate president, is negotiating the neutrality of the União Brasil-PP federation in the 2026 presidential election, distancing them from alliances that could strengthen Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). His actions are helping align the Centrão with Lula and reduce Bolsonarist support in key states.

item.title: Michelle acerta participação em programa eleitoral de Flávio e volta a gravar vídeos para aliadas em Brasília
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro confirmed her participation in Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral program, recording support videos for allies in Brasília and re-engaging in the campaign after family estrangement. She is also producing materials for Acre and Roraima candidacies while maintaining her Senate run in the DF. Tarcísio de Freitas and Alfredo Gaspar have been confirmed as key strategic supporters in Flávio's campaign.

item.title: Lula afasta Sidônio Palmeira de sua campanha eleitoral
item.description: President Lula has formally removed Sidônio Palmeira, head of the Secretariat of Social Communication (Secom) and the strategist behind his 2022 victory, from his 2026 electoral campaign. Despite the removal, Palmeira will continue working at the Planalto Palace and is expected to retain influence over Lula’s electoral strategy. The move reflects internal adjustments within the Workers’ Party campaign ahead of the next election.

item.title: Gelson Merísio votou em Bolsonaro em 2018 e agora é a aposta de Lula em SC
item.description: Former president of Santa Catarina's Legislative Assembly (Alesc) and businessman Gelson Merísio, who declared his vote for Jair Bolsonaro in 2018, is now being positioned as the head of President Lula's (PT) ticket for the 2026 gubernatorial race in Santa Catarina. His nomination reflects a PT strategy to broaden support in a traditionally conservative state by appealing to center and moderate right-wing voters. The move underscores Lula's efforts to build broad coalitions amid national political polarization.

item.title: Kassio reúne ministros em busca de consenso e quer decisão colegiada sobre IA de Bolsonaro; julgamento pode ocorrer semana que vem
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques convened a meeting with the Court's ministers to seek consensus on an AI-generated video showing Jair Bolsonaro supporting Flávio Bolsonaro. The goal is for the Court to issue a collegial decision, avoiding an individual ruling, with a possible judgment next week. The case will set a precedent for the 2026 elections, particularly regarding the use of deepfakes in campaigns.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não participa de sabatina da GloboNews
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, will not participate in the GloboNews and G1 sabatina after his campaign failed to confirm attendance within the deadline. The interview was scheduled for Monday, the 10th, but was canceled. His absence follows growing tensions between the candidate and traditional media outlets.

item.title: Caiado lança plano de segurança que prevê lei contra terrorismo doméstico; veja outras propostas
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), presidential candidate for 2026, unveiled a public security plan proposing to classify criminal factions as domestic terrorists, lower the age of criminal responsibility to 16 for specific crimes, and establish a Ministry of Public Security led by prosecutor Lincoln Gakiya. The plan includes minimum sentences of up to 45 years, parole eligibility only after serving 90% of the sentence, a special disciplinary regime for organized crime leaders, and the construction of 40 maximum-security prisons. It also addresses domestic violence, femicide, asset recovery, and anti-corruption measures.

item.title: O número que coloca em risco o projeto de reeleição de Lula
item.description: The BTG Nexus poll shows President Lula has a 48% disapproval rate, a major obstacle to his re-election bid, while his main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, faces 50% rejection. In a first-round simulation, Lula leads with 36% voting intention versus Flávio’s 29%, and in a runoff, Lula expands his lead to 47% against Flávio’s 44%. Other candidates — Caiado, Santos, and Zema — collectively garner only 5% in the first round.

item.title: O encontro de presidenciáveis que deve reunir Zema, Caiado e Renan Santos em Brasília
item.description: The National Union of Trade and Services Entities (UNECS) is hosting the 'Meeting with Presidential Candidates – Dialogue for Brazil’s Future' in Brasília, bringing together pre-candidates Augusto Cury (AVANTE), Renan Santos (Missão), Romeu Zema (NOVO) and former governor Ronaldo Caiado to discuss a manifesto with 14 strategic axes to boost productive sector competitiveness and reduce bureaucratic barriers. The event aims to influence government plans, aligning market expectations with future governance guidelines.

item.title: O dia D do TSE para o uso de inteligência artificial nas eleições
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques convened a closed-door meeting to address AI use in electoral events, particularly the deepfake of Bolsonaro at the PL convention that endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro. The goal is to establish guidelines on manipulated audio and video in voting intention polls and consider sanctions against Zero Um at the PT's request, given the ban on deepfakes in electoral propaganda effective August 16.

item.title: Evangélicos brasileiros se reúnem com parlamentares dos EUA para alertar sobre interferência nas eleições
item.description: Representatives of the Evangelical Front for the Rule of Law met with U.S. lawmakers in Washington to warn about potential foreign interference in Brazil's October 2026 elections. They delivered a letter expressing concerns over external influence on Brazil's electoral process. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Deputado trumpista da Flórida publica montagem de Lula capturado como Maduro
item.description: Florida Republican Congressman Carlos Giménez posted a montage depicting Brazilian President Lula as if he were Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro captured by the U.S., with the caption 'what awaits you'. The post was shared by Eduardo Bolsonaro and Paulo Figueiredo, Trump allies based in the U.S. who advocate for sanctions against Brazil. Giménez also accused Lula of 'castrocommunist' influence and hostility toward U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, following Rubio's announcement of 25% tariffs on Brazil.

item.title: A reação da campanha de Tarcísio à primeira pesquisa após o debate com Haddad
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' campaign reacted positively to the first post-debate poll, showing him leading with 50.6% voting intention versus Haddad's 33.6%, suggesting a potential first-round victory. The poll also revealed strong government approval at 63.3%, which the campaign interprets as public recognition of his governance. Despite confidence, the team urges calm in response to the results.

item.title: Flávio reunirá candidatos ao Senado para pedir que ampliem críticas ao STF durante campanha nos estados
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro will meet with around 50 Senate candidates he supports in Brasília to urge them to intensify criticism of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) in their state campaigns. The goal is to leverage these candidates' local structures to maintain his presidential presence nationwide, aligning Senate races with his campaign and coordinating joint strategies. The effort aims to secure a Senate majority capable of blocking or impeaching STF ministers, particularly Alexandre de Moraes, and includes backing candidates like Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP) despite the absence of a formal coalition.

item.title: Os momentos quentes dos principais debates aos governos estaduais
item.description: In the gubernatorial debate in São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad exchanged accusations regarding credibility, alleged ties to organized crime, and scientific denialism, with Haddad nationalizing the debate by referencing Lula and Bolsonaro. In Bahia, Jerônimo Rodrigues accused his opponent ACM Neto of mistreating him due to his Indigenous and Black identity, prompting a denied right-to-reply request.

item.title: Os anti-antifa - os fascistas voltam e revoltam (por Pedro Costa)
item.description: The text debates whether Getúlio Vargas's regime in Brazil can be considered fascist, noting that while it meets many fascist criteria — dictatorship, autocracy, militarism, suppression of opposition, social hierarchy, nationalism, and rejection of electoral democracy and political/economic freedoms — Vargas lacked a central party like Hitler or Mussolini. It also references his 1945 agreement with Luís Carlos Prestes and draws parallels between historical fascism and current trends, comparing them to antifa movements in the U.S. and the present Brazilian government.

item.title: Debate de SP tem risadas de Derrite e "intervenções" de Ricardo Nunes
item.description: The first electoral debate for the Government of São Paulo, held on August 9, highlighted the reactions of Guilherme Derrite (PP) and Ricardo Nunes (MDB), allies of Tarcísio de Freitas, who were present in the audience. Derrite became a target of Fernando Haddad’s (PT) criticism on public security, responding with ironic laughter and posting a video calling the PT candidate a 'liar'. Nunes also received mentions during the debate, underscoring the backing of Tarcísio’s allies amid PT attacks.

item.title: Como começou briga em debate que levou à demissão de cinegrafista da Globo
item.description: A GloboNews cameraman was fired after headbutting journalist Igor Carvalho of Brasil de Fato during a space dispute in the Band parking lot, prior to the debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad. The assault followed exchanges of insults and shoving, leaving Carvalho with a bleeding nose. Band security removed the cameraman, and Globo terminated his contract, condemning the violence.

item.title: Dois candidatos ao governo de MG declaram patrimônio zerado ao TSE
item.description: Two candidates for governor of Minas Gerais, Ben Mendes (Missão) and Túlio Lopes (PCB), declared zero assets to the Electoral Justice, according to the TSE system. Both have submitted their candidacy registrations, which are currently listed as 'awaiting judgment'. Mendes is a lawyer and influencer, while Lopes has prior electoral experience, having also declared zero assets in 2018.

item.title: Brasil reage a manobras de desinformação da Argentina, e Lula busca conversa com Trump
item.description: The Lula government has identified disinformation maneuvers in Argentina regarding the bilateral crisis and is seeking to clarify the situation to the Argentine public, emphasizing that the conflict originated from Javier Milei's speeches calling Lula a 'prisoner', 'thief', and 'corrupt'. Simultaneously, Lula aims to resume dialogue with Donald Trump to correct misinformation, such as the deforestation data used to justify U.S. trade tariffs, while recalling his positive relationship with the former U.S. president.

item.title: Globo demite cinegrafista após confusão no debate da Band
item.description: TV Globo fired the cameraman who assaulted a Brasil de Fato photographer during the São Paulo gubernatorial candidates' debate hosted by Band on Sunday night, the 9th. The network stated it terminated the contract of the temporary Globonews employee after reviewing the facts related to the incident.

item.title: ‘Flávio já devia ter escolhido e anunciado o seu Posto Ipiranga’, diz Valdemar
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL, criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for not yet announcing his potential Minister of Economy, stating it creates market insecurity and that he is 'wasting time'. He suggested economist Daniella Marques is likely to be invited to join the Esplanade of Ministries if Flávio wins the election. The remarks came as Flávio prepares to launch his campaign in Rio de Janeiro on the 16th, alongside his running mate Alfredo Gaspar.

item.title: Lula diz que defende investimentos na Defesa, mas o governo congela gastos com mísseis e foguetes
item.description: Lula publicly advocated for defense investments during visits to Avibras Aeroco and at the PT national convention, emphasizing Brazil's need to protect its vast borders, Amazon rainforest, and freshwater reserves. However, his administration froze R$ 300 million earmarked for rockets and missiles from Avibras, halting the first installment of a planned R$ 1.5 billion, five-year program for systems like the MTC-300 cruise missile and Astros modernization. The gap between rhetoric and budgetary action raises doubts about the sincerity and effectiveness of his defense policy.

item.title: Voto em trânsito: eleitor tem até 20 de agosto para solicitar
item.description: Voters wishing to cast an absentee ballot in the 2026 elections must apply by August 20, either online via the TSE portal or in person at any electoral office. The absentee voting option allows citizens to vote outside their home municipality, with voting rights varying by location: within the same state, all offices are eligible; outside the state, only the presidency is available. Changes or cancellations must also be submitted by August 20, and failure to vote requires justification via the e-Title app.

item.title: Associação do mercado financeiro leva agenda a campanhas e defende medidas para reduzir Custo Brasil
item.description: Anbima will present proposals for capital market development to all 2026 presidential candidates in meetings with their economic advisors, aiming to reduce Brazil's economic costs.

item.title: Lula lidera primeiro turno, mas empata com Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo, aponta Palver
item.description: Lula leads the first round with 44% to 45% against Flávio Bolsonaro's 40%, according to a Palver poll, with Renan Santos at 10%. In the second round, they are numerically tied, as Flávio consolidates the opposition while Lula maintains advantages among women, older voters, the educated, and in the Northeast. Religious cleavage is stark: Lula leads among Catholics and the non-religious, while Flávio dominates among evangelicals, reinforcing ideological and regional divides.

item.title: Globo toma atitude após cinegrafista agredir repórter em debate na Band
item.description: Globo fired the cameraman who assaulted Igor Carvalho, a reporter from Brasil de Fato, with a headbutt to the nose during a scuffle in the Band parking lot ahead of the São Paulo gubernatorial debate. The cameraman was a temporary worker for Globo News, and the network terminated his contract after reviewing the incident, stating it strongly condemns any form of violence.

item.title: Crusoé: Tarcísio vence Haddad no 1º turno, indica Ideia
item.description: Ideia poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) leading Fernando Haddad (PT) in the first round of the 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial race, with 51% voting intention versus Haddad’s 34%. Vera Lúcia (PSTU) follows with 3%. The poll was released on Monday, the 10th.

item.title: Depoimento indica trama petista para forjar acusação de estupro contra vice de Flávio
item.description: A Federal Legislative Police recorded an occurrence suggesting a plot involving Congressman Lindbergh Farias (PT) to fabricate a rape accusation against Congressman Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), the current running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro. The incident was reported in the Chamber of Deputies and raises concerns about political manipulation for electoral gain. If proven, the scheme could constitute false accusation and misuse of public resources.

item.title: Economia piora na pesquisa BTG, mas Lula ainda resiste ao mau humor do eleitor
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows 52% of voters now view Brazil's economy as bad or terrible, up 5 points in one week, while only 17% see it as good or excellent. Despite this sharp deterioration in national economic perception and future expectations, Lula maintains stable voting intentions: 40% in the first round and 47% in a potential runoff, all within the margin of error. His electoral resilience stems from the gap between negative views of the national economy and personal optimism — 45% believe their own financial situation will improve in the next six months.

item.title: Simões declara R$ 2,9 milhões em bens ao TSE; patrimônio cai ante 2022
item.description: Mateus Simões (PSD), candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, declared BRL 2.9 million in assets to the TSE in 2026, a 2.7% decrease from the BRL 2.98 million declared in 2022 when he was elected vice-governor. The largest asset is 50% of a house in Belo Horizonte valued at BRL 1.78 million, representing 61% of his total patrimony. The declaration includes company stakes, financial investments, gold, and other assets, with some items registered at zero value.

item.title: Fim da aposentadoria com salário dá a juízes ‘foro privilegiado anômalo’ no STF, dizem juristas
item.description: The extinction of salary-based retirement for judges by the STF created a new maximum penalty — availability with proposal of loss of office — transferring to the Supreme Court the prerogative to judge the definitive removal of office for all 19,000 judges nationwide, regardless of jurisdiction level or branch. This change constitutes an 'anomalous privileged forum,' according to legal experts, as it is not provided for by law and expands the STF’s power over the judiciary, benefiting judges accused of corruption, sale of rulings, and misconduct. The CNJ now has a mandatory review role, but the measure effectively grants judges functional immunity akin to that of authorities with forum by prerogative of function.

item.title: 2030 chega mais cedo em SP no debate entre Tarcísio e Haddad
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad held an intense debate in São Paulo, discussing national issues including the Lula and Bolsonaro administrations. The exchange of accusations and defenses created an atmosphere anticipating the 2030 presidential race, with both positioning themselves as central figures in a political future already unfolding.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula volta a liderar fora da margem contra Flávio no 1º turno
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leads the BTG/Nexus poll with a five-point percentage advantage over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the first round of the 2026 presidential election, exceeding the margin of error. The survey shows Lula retaining electoral strength amid growing opposition.

item.title: Para 44%, governo Lula é ruim ou péssimo, aponta BTG/Nexus; 34% consideram ótimo
item.description: BTG/Nexus poll shows 44% of voters rate Lula's government as bad or terrible, while 34% consider it excellent. The negative rating increased by 1 percentage point from the previous survey. The data reflects ongoing polarization in public perception of the current administration.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio mira ‘dor real’ de famílias para atacar Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign launches its electoral propaganda emphasizing the 'real pain' of low-income and middle-class families, linking urban violence and loss of purchasing power to Lula's government through ads depicting frustration over Bolsa Família dependence and declining education/health standards for children. The strategy leverages voter perception data (43% see economic deterioration) and avoids technical jargon to emotionally connect, tying the rise in public debt (from 71.7% to 81.9% of GDP) to food inflation and lack of investment.

item.title: Lula ou Flávio Bolsonaro: pesquisa mostra quem mais recebe votos de outros candidatos em um 2º turno
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll indicates that although Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) gains a majority of transferred votes from Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo) and Renan Santos (Missão) in a potential runoff against Lula (PT), the president still leads in the overall simulation with 47% versus 44%. Voters supporting Samara Martins favor Lula (61% vs 14%), while Augusto Cury's electorate shows a technical tie (38% vs 36%).

item.title: Flávio imita lives do pai, mas 55% na Quaest preveem vitória de Lula
item.description: A Quaest poll revealed that 55% of respondents believe Lula will win the 2026 presidential election, compared to only 28% who expect Flávio Bolsonaro to prevail. This reflects a strong 'expectation of power' favoring the president, which influences pragmatic voters to avoid candidates perceived as likely losers. Even among Flávio Bolsonaro's conservative base, 25% of his supporters do not believe he will win.

item.title: Campanha de Lula antecipa ataques a vice de Flávio e tenta ampliar desgaste de adversário no eleitorado feminino
item.description: Lula's campaign has preemptively attacked Alfredo Gaspar, Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate, over allegations of child rape to damage the ticket among female voters. The strategy links Flávio to Gaspar and Jair Bolsonaro, emphasizing Flávio's controversial remark about having daughters to care for him in old age and leveraging criticism from Michelle Bolsonaro. The goal is to exploit female electorate resistance (52% of voters) to the Bolsonaro ticket.

item.title: Zema e Caiado não dão segurança a seus eleitores, indica Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released Monday (10) shows that Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) have lost voter confidence, with a sharp decline in the share of voters certain about their first-round vote choice. Caiado’s supporters unwilling to change their vote dropped significantly, indicating weakness in their electoral bases. The survey suggests both candidates are failing to convey enough security to solidify support.

item.title: Ronaldo Caiado terá almoço com empresários para falar de reformas e economia
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado will lunch with business leaders in São Paulo to discuss economic reforms, legal security, infrastructure, and public safety. Organized by VIP Battistini, the event aims to foster direct dialogue between the private sector and presidential contenders on competitiveness and growth policies.

item.title: Novo marqueteiro define o slogan de Flávio Bolsonaro na campanha
item.description: Duda Lima, hired just 11 days ago as Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign marketer, created the slogan 'Brazil will win'. He explained the campaign is based on the 'V' shape in the name Flávio, using green and yellow to reinforce national identity and commitment to the country. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Flávio dará pontapé em sua campanha no dia 16 no RJ, enquanto Lula iniciará em São Paulo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will launch his campaign on the 16th in Rio de Janeiro, alongside his running mate Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), choosing the state as the birthplace of bolsonarism and his father Jair Bolsonaro’s electoral base. Simultaneously, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will hold his first campaign event on the same day in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), following the officialization of the Lula-Alckmin ticket, backed by PCdoB, PV, PSB, PDT, PSOL and Rede. The Lula vs. Flávio matchup will be central to the 2026 electoral contest.
